400	In any case, what I'm trying to say is that Abraham and Isaac were, Sarah and Abraham were
401	tumtumim.	"tumtumim" — keep as lines: see below
402	And Isaac and Rebecca were barren, and Jacob and Rachel were barren, and Leah too was barren,
403	as it says, "and HaShem saw that she was hated and opened her womb" — implying she was closed until He opened it. All of them
404	barren.
405	The Gemara asks, why?
406	Why?
407	It answers:
408	Because the Holy One, blessed be He, longs for the prayers of the tzaddikim.
409	So I understand that Isaac prayed for himself, but what is this: "And Isaac entreated HaShem opposite
410	Sarah — Rebecca — his wife, because she was barren."
411	Why, you were barren too, so what is "she was barren"?
412	Meaning she was barren, you weren't barren.
413	A big question.
414	So in years past I wrote several answers to this, several answers on this, and it was already printed in my book Merkavot
415	Argaman LaTorah.
416	Today I want to briefly go over the answers I brought and add another answer that only occurred to me today.
417	So of course it's not in the book, because it only occurred to me today.
418	Maybe one day when I publish the...
419	with the help of HaShem, when I publish my novel insights on the Torah in five volumes, which have multiplied and increased
420	the Torah, words of Torah fruitful and multiplying, then maybe we'll include this insight there too.
421	But after all, why is it written "because she was barren"?
422	So I said, in Bava Kama, page 92b, the Gemara says there: whoever prays for his fellow and needs the same thing
423	is answered first.
424	If you need something, when you pray for yourself, the attribute of judgment accuses you: he doesn't deserve it, he spoke lashon
425	hara, he doesn't have enough merits, he has transgressions.
426	But when you pray for your friend, the abundance descends straight to the friend.
427	By the way, what reaches the friend reaches you first, because you are the cause of opening the upper
428	spring, and then it goes to him.
429	And therefore whoever prays for his fellow and needs the same thing is answered first.
430	According to this, it is clear and simple why Isaac prays for her.
431	Because she was barren.
432	Meaning he prays for her.
433	He too was barren.
434	But he says, it's better to pray for her; if I pray for her, the Holy One, blessed be He, will answer me, and you'll see that it really is
435	so.
436	It is written there, "and HaShem was entreated by him." Why not by them?
437	Why not?
438	Because he was the one who prayed.
439	So whoever prays for his fellow and needs the same thing is answered first, and so it was; it seems brilliant to me.
